---
title: Boards & studio
description: Authoring boards on the studio canvas — the JSON document model under content/, paste-to-model, presets and vocab, export-as-MDX for design records, and the build-time validation gate.
---

The [studio](/studio) is gtm-docs' authoring surface: a canvas where you draw
the systems and a property panel where you describe them. Everything it edits
is a JSON document in the repo — which means every board is reviewable in a
pull request, and nothing is stored anywhere else.

## The document model

Boards live in `content/` as typed JSON documents, one file each, validated by
schema. Five kinds exist:

| Kind | Directory | What it holds |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `board` | `content/boards/` | A flow map: nodes (systems) and edges (data movement). `icp-pipeline.board.json` is the flagship. |
| `app` | `content/apps/` | One card per vendor system (HubSpot, Clay, Snowflake, …) with its category and profile. |
| `preset` | `content/presets/` | Object field templates (`hubspot.contact`, `clay.row`, …) — the fields, types, and **PII** flags the studio infers data models from. |
| `vocab` | `content/vocab/` | The controlled vocabularies: motions (cross-sell, upsell, …), mechanisms (api-pull, enrichment-run, …), app categories. |
| `system-record` | `content/systems/` | The structured record behind a design record (coming with paydirt 0.5.0). |

A **board** is drawn in a grammar every reader learns once: card archetypes
say what a system *is* — **source** (where data is born), **processor**
(shapes it), **destination** (where it lands), **consumer** (the revenue
motion that uses it) — and every arrow says how the data moves (mechanism),
how often (cadence), and what travels (payload). Where an arrow crosses a
credential boundary it carries the credential **name** (`SNOWFLAKE_RO_KEY`) —
a name, never a value.

## The canvas

The studio shell is a board selector, a left palette of app cards, the center
canvas, and a right property panel for whatever is selected. Drag to pan,
scroll to zoom, use the minimap to jump around, and click any card or arrow
for its full detail. Boards embedded in docs (`<Board src="icp-pipeline" />`
on the [ICP pipeline record](/docs/systems/icp-pipeline)) are the same live
canvas, not screenshots.

The editor state *is* the document JSON: saves go through validation and land
in `content/` as deterministic bytes (sorted keys, stable formatting), so diffs
stay readable. A crash-recovery draft lives in browser storage and nowhere
else.

Saves are **local-first**: the write path exists only in development (`pnpm
--filter gtm-docs dev`). Deployed instances mount the studio read-only with a
clone-the-repo affordance — see [deploy your own](/docs/build/deployment).

## From paste to data model

Paste raw JSON (an API response, a Clay table export) or CSV into
paste-to-model and the studio infers entities, field types, and PII flags,
then stages them for review — rename, fix types, toggle PII — before anything
is committed to the board. The `content/presets/` templates give the same
starting point for known objects, and the vocabularies keep motions and
mechanisms from drifting between records.

Model boards export as **copy-as-MDX**: a ready-to-paste `<DataModel … />`
snippet for section 4 of a design record. Flow boards are embedded directly
with `<Board src="…" />`.

## The validation gate

Every document under `content/` is validated on every build — `prebuild` runs
the content walk (`pnpm --filter gtm-docs validate`), so a malformed board or a
schema-drifted preset fails CI before it ships. The studio's save path runs
the same validation, which means an invalid document cannot land in `content/`
through either door. Docs pages under `content/docs/` are excluded from the
walk: their `meta.json` files are page-tree configuration, not documents.

## Adding a record

The full path from blank canvas to published page is documented in
[Systems — adding a record](/docs/systems): author the MDX file, build or
paste the data model in the studio, embed the board or copy the MDX, and add
the page to `systems/meta.json` so the sidebar picks it up.
